text:
jordan: heads-up: after last night's kernel-cost change I'm seeing host-side p99 regression for very short requests (1-6 tokens). p99 from ~5.9ms -> ~14.3ms on canary cluster.

emily: timeline? which deploy?

jordan: infra-bot shows host-runtime v3.13.2 rolled at 02:12Z. regression correlates with selector now favoring wide_attention for predicted higher throughput.

rao: any samples/profiles yet?

jordan: grabbed a 30s perf sample on a canary host, top stacks trimmed: 
```
Samples: 1200 of event 'cycles'
  41%  host-runtime: memcpy_loop
  20%  host-runtime: grpc_readv
  12%  host-runtime: tokenizer_heap_alloc
   9%  host-runtime: kv_miss_serialize
   7%  kernel: wide_attention_dispatch
  11%  other
```

ben: memcpy_loop that high for tiny payloads suggests repeated small copies in proto/unpack or KV metadata assembly. did batching heuristics change?

jordan: yes, heuristic now estimates batchable window based on recent seq_len histogram which biases toward grouping short requests and triggers the wide path hoping for GPU efficiency. but when kv-hit is low we do more host-side work per request and the wide path's prep copies dominate.

emily: so two interacting factors: (A) mispredicted batch grouping, (B) wide_kernel prep cost being nontrivial for tiny requests when kv misses.

rao: quick mitigation options: 
- add a lightweight kernel_cost_estimate(tokens, kv_hit) to selector and prefer narrow for tiny tokens when kv_hit < 0.6
- throttle fragmenter so proxy coalesces outgoing frames for small responses (fewer syscalls)
- pool small buffers for proto unpack to avoid allocator churn

ben: i can flip a runtime flag to re-enable coalescing on canary: --egress-coalesce-ms=5 --min-coalesce-bytes=300. that should reduce grpc_readv/syscall overhead.

jordan: please do. and i'll push a selector guard: if tokens <= 8 && kv_hit < 0.6 -> force NARROW_FAST. code snippet: 
```
// selector hint
if (req.tokens <= 8 && telemetry.kv_hit_rate < 0.6) {
  hint = KERNEL_NARROW_LOW_OVERHEAD;
}
```

emily: also add a trace span around memcpy_loop so we can attribute to exact callsites (proto unpack vs kv key flatten).

ops: note: deploy bot shows v3.13.2 canary on 5 hosts. flipping flags only affects 2 of them (canary group).

ben: microbench that helped us earlier: writev tail for 128B vs 512B frames: p99(128B)=6.1ms, p99(512B)=1.3ms under same QPS. small frames really kill tail.

rao: good to know. after enabling coalesce on 2 canaries i re-ran perf: memcpy_loop dropped to 22% (from 41%), grpc_readv down to 9%. overall p99 for 1-6 tokens fell from 14.3ms -> 6.8ms. still above baseline but much better.

jordan: thanks. i rolled the kernel hint patch to one canary host as well, combined result: p99 now ~5.4ms which is within noise.

emily: plan for next steps: 
1) keep coalesce flag on canary and promote if green for 1h soak
2) ship selector kernel_cost_estimate as opt-in runtime flag; default to old behavior but allow ops to enable fallback for tiny requests
3) implement pooled arena for proto/unpack in follow-up (prealloc 4KB slabs reused)
4) add metrics: host.rpc.coalesce.effective_bytes, host.kernel.selector.reason (labels: cost_estimate,kvcache_hint,manual)

ben: i've opened PR with the coalesce metric + docs for flags.

ops: infra-bot: deploy-service: host-runtime v3.13.2 (canary: 5 hosts) :white_check_mark:

jordan: soaking 1h now with both mitigations. I'll post flamegraphs and perf diff (before/after) to the thread. if soak stays green, we promote and open follow-ups for allocator arena + selector telemetry.

emily: longer-term we should also refine the selector model to include expected host-side work delta on kv_miss path (serialize cost, extra memcpys) so kernel choice is not GPU-only.

rao: agree. i'll sketch an estimator and run a small simulation on historical traces to see misprediction rate.

jordan: quick note: found one weird case where batching grouped 12 tiny requests into a single wide batch and wide_kernel added ~900us of prep per request because of extra KV marshalling. added an assertion in the selector test to avoid grouping >8 tokens when kv_hit < 0.5.

emily: solid. thanks everyone. once we merge the telemetry + arena follow-up we can remove the runtime knobs. :eyes:
